clue.text: Structure of pollarded tree

indicators.note: pollarding lops off the top growth, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a larch is a conifer

explanation.surface: A gardener admires the shape a cut-back tree has taken.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the top of the tree is its first letter, so pollarding the larch removes the L.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch is a curved built form spanning an opening, a kind of construction or edifice.

clue.text: Rank obscenity fully raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising letters makes them read from bottom to top

parts.note: dirt is smutty, obscene talk
up means completely, as in 'eat up'

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a crude piece of filth has been held high for all to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like a position in a hierarchy, but here it is the adjective meaning foul-smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe something rotten that gives off a foul, decaying smell.

clue.text: Half of shipment for food shop

indicators.note: taking half of a word means dropping the other half of its letters

parts.note: a delivery is a consignment of goods

explanation.surface: Part of a consignment is destined for a grocer's.
explanation.walkthrough: The eight-letter word is cut to its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling cooked meats, cheeses and prepared foods.

clue.text: Peter out with Mark and Jack?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to tire or lose energy
second meaning: to mark or highlight something for attention
third meaning: a small banner flown at a ship's bow

explanation.surface: Peter heads out with two friends, Mark and Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make three men's names; each phrase is really a separate meaning of one word, and the question mark admits the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb for weakening, a verb for marking for attention, and a noun for a banner such as a jack.

clue.text: Turn up chinos and incorporate trendy sewer's accessory

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take something inside, so one piece is put within another
to turn things is to change their order, so these letters get rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Advice to roll up your trousers and add a fashionable item for a tailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' looks like a phrasal verb about trouser hems, but 'Turn' alone is the signal and 'up' is fodder. IN goes in after the first letter of the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewer here is someone who sews, and a pincushion holds the pins and needles used in needlework.

clue.text: Report of simple child's plaything

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: bare means plain or unadorned

explanation.surface: A report on an uncomplicated toy for a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: A teddy is the child's plaything meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A teddy bear is the classic soft cuddly toy that small children carry around.

clue.text: Sister's pinching wheels for some footballers

indicators.note: to pinch is to grip tight, so one piece clutches another inside it

parts.note: SR is the abbreviation for Sister
the possessive ending kept as written
a trike is a tricycle

explanation.surface: A nun steals a car for some of the team's players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinching' suggests theft, but it means the outer letters hold the bike; the 's is part of the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Strikers are forward players in soccer whose main job is scoring goals.

clue.text: Head off out to lunch with host

indicators.note: with its head off, a word loses its first letter

parts.note: out to lunch is slang for crazy, which is barmy

explanation.surface: Someone sets off for a lunch date with the person entertaining them.
explanation.walkthrough: Barmy is British slang for mad. 'Host' looks like a person entertaining guests; it is the old sense of a multitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is an archaic word for an armed force, as in the heavenly host or the hosts of Midian.

clue.text: Way to eliminate unsatisfactory service in game

indicators.note: to eliminate something is to get rid of it, so those letters come out

parts.note: roulette is a casino game
in tennis a let is a serve that must be replayed

explanation.surface: A tennis tip on cutting out poor serves during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is tennis, which supplies the let but not the game: the game is spun at a casino.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is the course or road taken to get somewhere, which is a way.

clue.text: Irish province has church for new city

indicators.note: one thing standing in place of another, so a letter is swapped out

parts.note: Leinster is the eastern province of Ireland
CE is the Church of England
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: An Irish region gets a church in place of a new town.
explanation.walkthrough: The N of the province is replaced by CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicester is a large city in the English East Midlands.

clue.text: Husband going astray with school member

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
erring means straying from the right path

explanation.surface: A married man is having an affair with a teacher or pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' is not a place of learning but a shoal of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Herring swim in huge shoals, so one of these fish is a member of a school.

clue.text: Confirm playground's back in repair

indicators.note: going back means running the other way, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground
rectify means put right; this is what follows its opening three letters

explanation.surface: A council confirms that the play area's rear section is under repair.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb RECTIFY, to repair, begins with the British word for a park; turn that part round in place.
explanation.definitionFit: To certify is to attest formally that something is true, which is to confirm it.

clue.text: Bleaches hairstyles

definitions.meaning: first meaning: loses or takes away colour
second meaning: haircuts that taper short at the sides

explanation.walkthrough: Bleach and haircuts suggest one salon visit; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb describes colour paling away, and the noun is a barber's cut graduated from short to long.

clue.text: Tree has shoot cut

indicators.note: something cut is shortened, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to fire a gun is to shoot

explanation.surface: A tree has had one of its new growths pruned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' looks like a sprouting stem, fitting the tree; it is the verb for using a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: The fir is a common evergreen conifer.

clue.text: Change working time

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to move or alter
second meaning: a set period of work

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an instruction to alter office hours; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means move or alter; as a noun it is the period an employee is rostered on.

clue.text: Part of computer described by web user

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the letters sit enclosed in the words

parts.note: spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A web surfer explains a component of their PC.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Web user' suggests an internet surfer, or a spider; it is just a string of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus is the set of circuits carrying data between a computer's components.

clue.text: Bad tempered cook called out brother

parts.note: a black mood is a foul temper

indicators.note: something called out is spoken, so it is taken by its sound

parts.note: a fryer is one who fries food

explanation.surface: A grumpy chef shouts at a sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brother' looks like a sibling, but it is a member of a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominican friars were called Black Friars for their black cloaks, and a friar is addressed as Brother.

clue.text: Prow of icebreaker blocking a dock

indicators.note: to block a passage is to stand in it, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: per means a, as in 'once per day'

indicators.note: a prow is a ship's front, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: The bow of an icebreaker is stuck, preventing access to a harbour berth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' meaning per is the less obvious step: three miles a day is three miles per day.
explanation.definitionFit: A pier is a landing stage where ships tie up, which is a dock.

clue.text: Animal seen in the outskirts of Pasadena

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges of a town, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: its first letter
outskirts are two edges, one letter and the other
its last letter

explanation.surface: A creature is spotted on the edge of a Californian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The outskirts are P and A, and the answer is that phrase written out: P AND A.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda is a black-and-white bear native to China.

clue.text: Strange cyst removed from pelvic bone

indicators.note: something removed is taken out, so those letters go

parts.note: the sacrum is the bone at the base of the spine
a sac is a cyst or pouch

explanation.surface: An odd cyst has been surgically taken off a hip bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' looks like an adjective for the cyst, but it is the definition; rum is old British slang for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage rum is an adjective meaning odd or peculiar, as in 'a rum business'.

clue.text: A gym Noah built in wood

indicators.note: to build is to put parts together, so these letters are assembled anew

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Noah, famous for building the ark of wood, constructed a gymnasium in timber.
explanation.walkthrough: Noah built the ark, which makes 'built' read naturally as construction.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahogany is a hard reddish-brown tropical timber used for fine furniture.

clue.text: Catch a flier briefly returning meal

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so everything is read backwards
something brief is cut short, so the word loses its end

parts.note: to nail someone is to catch them
taken as written
a tit is a small bird

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a quick bite before a flight home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' suggests an aircraft passenger, but it is a bird, shortened to TI. 'Meal' fits as in 'going for an Italian'.
explanation.definitionFit: Going out for an Italian means eating a dinner of Italian food, so the word stands for a meal.

clue.text: A lot of water in small local river

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
ea is a dialect word for a river

explanation.surface: There is plenty of water in a little stream nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' marks a dialect word: EA is a regional term for a river or stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea is a vast expanse of salt water, so it is a great amount of it.

clue.text: Colonist and Australian conservationists

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for Australian
the NT is the National Trust, a British heritage charity

explanation.surface: A settler and some Australian environmentalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colonist' looks like a human settler; it is an insect living in a colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Ants live in large organised colonies, so each insect is a member of one.

clue.text: Try to extract everything from onion

indicators.note: to extract is to pull out, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: a shallot is a small onion
all means everything

explanation.surface: A cook attempts to get every bit of flavour out of an onion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' reads as a verb but is the noun, as in 'have a try'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot is an attempt, as in 'have a shot at it', which is a try.

clue.text: Keystone Kops part reviewed for Ryan Gosling role

indicators.note: to review is to look back over, so the letters run backwards
a part is a portion, so only some consecutive letters are taken

parts.note: spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A critic reviews a slapstick part as an audition for a Hollywood star.
explanation.walkthrough: The Keystone Kops were silent-film comic policemen; 'part' and 'role' both look like acting talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Gosling played the doll companion in the 2023 film Barbie, so this is the character he portrayed.

clue.text: New York ward features in key warning

indicators.note: to feature in something is to appear within it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard
ER is the American emergency room of a hospital

explanation.surface: A New York hospital ward plays a key part in raising the alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the American term, so the New York tag points to it rather than a British casualty ward.
explanation.definitionFit: An alert is a signal of danger given in advance, which is a warning.

clue.text: Trump's rating: Standard

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a junior officer rank in the US Navy, the President's navy
second meaning: a flag flown by a ship

explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump's rating' looks like an approval poll; it means a rank in the American navy. Strictly a rating is a non-commissioned sailor, so the term is used loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US Navy this is the lowest commissioned officer rank, and as a noun it also means a flag or banner.

clue.text: Composer welcomes old driver

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Richard Wagner, the German composer
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A composer greets an elderly chauffeur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' seems to describe the driver, but it only supplies a letter; Wagner is the German opera composer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagoner is the person who drives a horse-drawn wagon, so a carter or teamster.

clue.text: Block Liberal legislation in U-turn

indicators.note: a U-turn sends you back the way you came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal
a law is a piece of legislation

explanation.surface: The Liberals obstruct a bill after the government changes its mind.
explanation.walkthrough: A political U-turn is a reversal of policy, which is exactly what happens to the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall is a barrier, and a block is something that obstructs a way through.

clue.text: European native stands up to see informer

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up turns the letters to read from bottom to top

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
a native son is someone born in a place

explanation.surface: A local European rises to meet a police spy.
explanation.walkthrough: Nose is British slang for a police informer, an old underworld term.
explanation.definitionFit: In criminal slang a nose is someone who sniffs out and passes on information to the police.

clue.text: Duke and German boy meeting a king for curry

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for Duke
Hans is a typical German boy's name
taken as written
K is king in chess and cards

explanation.surface: A nobleman and a German lad join a monarch for an Indian meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meeting' simply strings the pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: Dhansak is a Parsi curry of meat cooked with lentils, common on British Indian restaurant menus.

clue.text: River and river animal

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A river, and a creature that lives by rivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River animal' reads as a single phrase like otter; the second 'river' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The deer is a hoofed mammal, the stag being the male.

clue.text: Expert filling barrel with beer — quite the reverse

indicators.note: a filling sits inside something, so one piece is put within another
this swaps the roles stated, so the outer and inner pieces trade places

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
B is an abbreviation for barrel

explanation.surface: A specialist pours beer into a cask, or rather the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the expert fills the barrel; the closing phrase flips the containment, so the barrel goes into the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Expert as an adjective means skilled, and able means competent or skilful.

clue.text: Christopher Lee finally getting aircraft

parts.note: Kit is a short form of Christopher

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: The horror actor Christopher Lee at last boards a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: The actor's full name invites a film reference, but the two names are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A kite is a light frame flown in the wind, and in old RAF slang it also meant a plane.

clue.text: Gets head in painting

parts.note: to land something is to get it, as in landing a job
a cape is a headland

explanation.surface: Someone manages to fit a head into a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' suggests a portrait, the opposite kind of painting; here it is a coastal headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a painting of natural scenery, one of the main genres of picture.

clue.text: Frivolous rest day

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to settle or come down on
third meaning: daylight, the time when the sun is up

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a lazy day off; each word is instead a separate meaning of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means trivial as an adjective, alight or settle as a verb, and daytime brightness as a noun.
